title: Design System: Student activities companion (working title)

display.purpose: Page titles: What's on, Sign in; the student's name on Profile (4.5rem / 3.25rem, one step smaller past 18 characters).

date-line.purpose: Weekday and date on every poster and poster header; the poster's headline.

headline.purpose: Week group headings, side-panel spots figure, sign-in option headings; Profile's stub titles (1.5rem / 1.375rem) and open-stub panel heading (1.875rem / 1.625rem).

title.purpose: Activity titles on posters and the detail header.

fact.purpose: Deciding facts on posters; never below 1rem.

label.purpose: Fact-sheet labels, hints, field errors; never a deciding fact; the Saved confirmation on Profile (750).

billing.purpose: Area names on the summary line-up at four fixed rank sizes (4.5/3.25/2.25/1.5rem; phones 2.75/2.125/1.625/1.25rem).

setting.purpose: A setting row's label on Profile, normal width and sentence case, over a 0.9375rem Paper Dim description (58ch).

outlines.name: focus-ring
outlines.purpose: Keyboard focus on every interactive element; Paper on the wall.

outlines.name: poster-hover
outlines.purpose: Poster hover and focus-within, in place of a lift.

outlines.name: stub-open
outlines.purpose: The open Profile stub (aria-expanded); Warm Rule on hover.

motion.name: paste-up
motion.value: opacity 0.2 to 1, translateY 6px to 0, 180ms ease-out, 25ms stagger capped at 8
motion.purpose: Posters, to-log tickets and summary line-up rows on load and filter or range change only.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour and border transitions on buttons, tabs, fields, the switch track and knob, the stub outline.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.value: scale 1.7 to 0.95 (ease-in) then to 1 (ease-out), keeps rotate(7deg), opacity 0 to 1 in the first half, 300ms
motion.purpose: GOING stamp after joining, on the poster and the activity header; on Profile, a stub's state stamp when its word changes (OFF to ON or LINKED). Once.

motion.name: ticket-out
motion.value: opacity to 0, scale to 0.94, 220ms ease-in after 320ms; remaining tickets slide over the gap 240ms ease-out (FLIP)
motion.purpose: The ticket just logged leaves the to-log strip after saving. Once.

motion.name: ink-in
motion.value: clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0), 380ms ease-out, 250ms delay, starts when the day is 90% on screen
motion.purpose: The saved day's ink and photo paste into the calendar after saving. Once.

motion.name: bar-grow
motion.value: clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0), 520ms ease-out, 45ms stagger; totals fade up 4px over 220ms after 300ms
motion.purpose: Summary columns on load and range change.

motion.name: pick-dim
motion.purpose: Summary: what was not picked steps back.

motion.name: saved-flash
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, 150ms ease; held 1.8s, then cleared
motion.purpose: The Going Mint Saved word beside a setting on Profile after the server confirms a change.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Wall to two columns; facts stack; side panel 300px. Journal day panel drops below the calendar.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: One column, compact posters, one scrolling row of area tabs, side panel above content. Tickets scroll in one row; calendar keeps seven columns, ink only; day panel and entry header bleed to the edges. Profile stubs go 2x2; the header's name and Sign out give way to a round profile icon, and Sign out moves onto the Profile page.

breakpoints.name: small-phone
breakpoints.purpose: The product name hides from the header so the four nav links fit on one line; Browse is home.

futureSurfaces: Admin: add activity form and CSV import

photoTreatment.name: duotone
photoTreatment.value: img { filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.15) brightness(1.05); mix-blend-mode: multiply; } on a var(--ink) ground
photoTreatment.purpose: Photos on the wall: poster photo bands and logged calendar day cells.

photoTreatment.name: natural
photoTreatment.purpose: Photos inside panels (day panel entries, form thumbnails) and on the activity page.

narrative.overview:
The week's activities are pasted up as gig posters on a dark wall, the kind outside *SCAPE or the Esplanade. The date is the headline: set in Archivo at its narrowest and heaviest, so what is soon reads from across the room. Each of the four areas is one flat spot ink, and every poster is printed on its ink in near-black. Everything around the posters (header, filters, side panels, forms) stays on the wall: near-black ground, warm off-white paper type, thin warm rules.

The system is flat and printed. Depth comes only from ink against wall; there are no gradients, textures or shadows. Type width is the main expressive lever: poster type runs condensed (wdth 62) and uppercase, titles slightly wider (wdth 76), and every fact a student must read to decide runs at normal width and body size or larger. The poster world never outranks usability: posters stay compact on phones, Join sits in the same corner of every poster, and full or closed activities say so twice, with a stamp and a disabled button.

Motion is one gesture: posters paste up once on load and on filter change. Three moments confirm an action the same way: joining presses the GOING stamp on, saving an entry clears its to-log ticket and pastes that day's ink in, and changing a setting re-presses the state stamp on its stub. Nothing else moves beyond state transitions.

This system replaces the retired MRT arrival-board world (kept in git history). The journal is the first extension built inside it: the wall's own month calendar, where each logged day is pasted in its area's ink and each missed log is an empty dashed slot, with small ink tickets for what still needs logging and a one-page entry form under a poster header. The summary is the second: the four areas billed like a gig poster's line-up, type size as rank, the headliner biggest in its ink and an area with no hours set smallest in Paper Faint with a way to find one; under it, hours per month as stacked ink columns and the entries behind each area. Profile is the third: the student's settings as four stubs stamped with their state (OFF, ON, LINKED) in the posters' own stamp, paper when a setting is on and dark on the wall when it is off, so a glance says how everything stands before a tap opens one. It must extend the same way, without new worlds, to the remaining planned surfaces: the reflection compiler, the optional award tracker, and admin. No components exist for those yet; build them from the wall, paper type, spot inks and the components below.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black wall, warm off-white paper ink, one flat spot ink per area.
The date line is the headline: Archivo 900, wdth 62, uppercase, tight leading.
Posters are square-cornered ink blocks; controls are pills; text fields are gently rounded.
Flat throughout: no gradients, textures or shadows.
Status is printed: angled FULL, CLOSED, GOING stamps; on Profile, OFF, ON and LINKED on settings stubs.
Deciding facts at body size or larger, tabular numerals everywhere.
Photos print as duotone in the area ink on the wall, and in natural colour inside panels and on the activity page.
On the journal calendar, ink means logged and a dashed slot means still to log.
On the summary, type size is rank: four fixed billing sizes, set by hours.
On Profile, a paper stub means a setting is on; a dark stub with a dashed edge means it is off or absent.

rules.name: The One Ink Per Area Rule
rules.body: Each spot ink belongs to exactly one area and is used only to identify it. Never use a spot ink for status, emphasis or decoration; states use the wall's own state colors.

rules.name: The Printed In Black Rule
rules.body: Anything on a spot ink is Press Black (on-ink), never paper or another ink. The only reversal is the closing-soon fact, which knocks the poster's ink out of a black band.

rules.name: The Duotone On The Wall Rule
rules.body: On the wall (poster photo bands, logged calendar day cells) a photo is printed in greyscale multiplied into its area's ink, so it reads as part of the poster. Inside panels (the day panel's entry photos, form thumbnails) and on the activity page the same photo shows in its natural colour. Text never sits on a photo.

rules.name: The Ink Type On The Wall Rule
rules.body: A spot ink may print directly on the wall as type only for an area's own name, in billing type (900, wdth 62, uppercase, 1.25rem or larger), as on the summary line-up. This is identification, so it sits inside One Ink Per Area; it is not on an ink, so Printed In Black does not apply. Every other area label on the wall stays paper type with the 11-13px ink dot, and numbers beside an inked name stay paper. An area with nothing to identify (no hours) drops its ink for Paper Faint.

rules.name: The Date Is The Headline Rule
rules.body: On every poster and poster header, the date line is the largest type. Titles come second.

rules.name: The Deciding Facts Rule
rules.body: Spots left and the closing date are at body size (1rem) or larger on every viewport, never small print. Spots left leads at 1.125rem.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Condensed width (wdth 62-76) is for dates, titles and headings in uppercase. Facts, controls and prose use normal width and sentence case.

rules.name: The Size Is Rank Rule
rules.body: On the line-up an area's name size is its billing rank by hours, from four fixed sizes only. Areas tied on hours share a size; an area with no hours always takes the smallest. On phones a long name wraps to two lines rather than shrinking below its rank size. The hours and count beside it stay normal width and right-aligned, so the numbers read at full size whatever the billing.

rules.name: The Three On A Phone Rule
rules.body: At 760px and below a poster is compact (16px padding, 3.25rem date on one line, 1.375rem title, area name hidden) so about three posters are visible per screen.

rules.name: The Seven Columns On A Phone Rule
rules.body: On phones the calendar keeps all seven columns; day cells drop their photos and show ink only, the Log mark shrinks to 0.6875rem and the flag to 18px. The to-log tickets become one 236px-wide scrolling row that bleeds to the screen edges, and the chosen day's panel opens below the grid, edge to edge.

rules.name: The One Row Of Areas Rule
rules.body: On phones the area pills sit in one horizontally scrolling row that bleeds to the screen edges, with no visible scrollbar; the cut-off last pill shows there is more. The search field and a 128px date select share one row below it.

rules.name: The Pasted Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, gradient or texture on any surface. A poster announces itself with ink, not elevation.

rules.name: The Same Corner Rule
rules.body: Join (or its disabled stand-in, or the Going tag with Leave) always sits bottom right of the poster, in the poster foot, regardless of how long the title or facts run.

rules.name: The Said Twice Rule
rules.body: A full or closed activity shows a stamp and a disabled button whose label gives the reason (Full, Closed, Sign-up closed). Never hide the button, never use colour alone.

rules.name: The Paste-Up Rule
rules.body: Posters, to-log tickets and summary line-up rows fade up from 0.2 opacity and 6px below over 180ms (ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), staggered 25ms each and capped at the eighth poster, on load and filter or range change only. Details panel rows paste up the same way when a pick opens them. Reduced motion removes it. The calendar and the day panel do not animate, except as below.

rules.name: The Grow Rule
rules.body: On load and range change the summary's columns grow up from the baseline (clip-path wiping in from the bottom over 520ms, ease-out, 45ms apart left to right), and each total fades up 4px over 220ms as its column lands. Picking fades other columns or segments over 150ms. Nothing else on the chart moves, and reduced motion removes all of it.

rules.name: The Confirm Rule
rules.body: Motion may confirm an action the student just took, once, where they are looking. Joining presses the GOING stamp onto the poster (and the activity header): it drops from 1.7x to 0.95x and settles at 1x over 300ms, keeping its 7° tilt. Saving an entry from a ticket shows that ticket once more, fades it to 0.94x after 320ms, and slides the remaining tickets over the gap in 240ms (on phones the strip scrolls to it first). The saved day's ink and photo then wipe up from the bottom over 380ms, starting only once the day is on screen. Changing a setting re-presses its stub's stamp with the same 300ms stamp-in, only when the stamp's word changes (OFF to ON, OFF to LINKED). Nothing repeats, nothing loops, and reduced motion removes all of it.

rules.name: The Filled Or Dashed Rule
rules.body: On the journal calendar a past day the student went to is either filled with its area's ink (logged) or a dashed empty slot marked Log (still to log). Ink on the calendar means logged and nothing else.

rules.name: The Paper Is On Rule
rules.body: On Profile a stub is printed on Paper in Press Black when its setting is on or linked, and goes dark on the wall (Wall Shadow, paper type, a 2px dashed Paper Faint edge) when it is off or absent. Stubs never take an area ink; an area's ink appears on Profile only as the 11px dot on its area pill.

rules.name: The Long Name Rule
rules.body: The student's name on Profile is display type at 4.5rem (3.25rem on phones); a name over 18 characters steps down one size, to 3.25rem (2.25rem on phones). It wraps anywhere and balances, and never truncates.

rules.name: The Stamped State Rule
rules.body: Every Profile setting shows how it stands on its stub before any tap: the stamp's word, paper or dark, and a sub line in words. Never hide a setting's state behind a tap.

rules.name: The Needs Telegram Rule
rules.body: While Telegram is unlinked, every reminder renders off and disabled under the Needs Telegram box, and the Reminders stub reads OFF, "Needs Telegram". The choices the student saved are kept and come back once Telegram is linked.

dos: **Do** give every activity surface its area's spot ink and print on it in Press Black.
**Do** set dates as the largest type on a poster: Archivo 900, wdth 62, uppercase.
**Do** keep spots left and the closing date at 1rem or larger on every viewport.
**Do** keep posters compact on phones so about three show per screen.
**Do** put Join in the bottom-right corner of every poster.
**Do** show full and closed as a stamp plus a disabled button that names the reason.
**Do** keep area filters in one scrolling row on phones.
**Do** design slow, empty and failed loads as states on the wall (skeletons, the waking-up note, dashed empty frame, coral error frame).
**Do** print photos as duotone in the area ink on the wall, and show them in natural colour inside panels and on the activity page.
